title: Affective Computing and Emotional Data: Challenges and Implications in Privacy Regulations, The AI Act, and Ethics in Large Language Models

bias_targets.methodology: Theoretical evaluation and literature review of emotional stereotyping (e.g., assumptions that women express emotions more intensely) and recognition accuracy disparities in affective computing systems.
Theoretical analysis of disparities in emotion recognition accuracy stemming from marginalized or absent ethnicities in training datasets.
Literature review-based assessment of performance disparities in emotion recognition systems across different age groups.
Ethical and theoretical evaluation of applying Western-centric (WEIRD) psychological models to diverse cross-cultural populations with varying emotional display rules and expressions.

Theoretical evaluation of accessibility barriers and systematic misinterpretation risks for individuals with neurological differences (e.g., autism) or physical limitations (e.g., Parkinson's disease) who exhibit atypical emotional expressions.
